metadata.degree_name: MPhil specialising in Insolvency and Business Rescue (Coursework)

module_catalog.name: Comparative and international insolvency principles 821
module_catalog.content: The aim of the module is to provide students with the required background regarding the principles and theory of the South African insolvency system within an international and comparative context. The outcome of this module is to equip students with an advanced knowledge of the issues related to this ever-evolving industry.

module_catalog.name: Corporate liquidation and business rescue regulation 822
module_catalog.content: The aim of the module is to provide students with advanced knowledge regarding the principles of corporate liquidation and rescue including the administration of an insolvent or financially distressed estate.

module_catalog.name: Research methodology 804
module_catalog.content: This essential module serves as the methodological foundation for MPhil programmes in Management Sciences. It equips students with the skills to design, execute, and evaluate rigorous research across different paradigms. The module is delivered in a blended format, offering flexibility for working professionals, and incorporates intensive in-person workshops, guided online sessions, and personalised consultations.

module_catalog.name: Research Methodology 815
module_catalog.content: Strong emphasis on market research, quantification of the market but also a basis for academic publications and a doctorate.

module_catalog.name: Distressed business assessment 821
module_catalog.content: The aim of this module is to equip students to explore the concepts, theories, patterns and recent cases of the four stages of corporate sickness: decline, distress, insolvency and bankruptcy. It examines contemporary product, production, accounting, financial, marketing, alliance and joint venture-based turnaround strategies. The module provides students with a perspective on identifying and remedying turnaround business situations, that is, established businesses experiencing operational, financial and managerial difficulties. Students learn, from the viewpoint of a general manager, how to distinguish between "troubled" and "crisis" companies and how to use both qualitative and quantitative tools to effect solutions.

module_catalog.name: Financial distress assessment 822
module_catalog.content: The aim of this module is to equip students to explore modern research in corporate financial distress. Topics covered include financial distress identification and prediction, the link between distress and macroeconomic conditions, and financial bubbles. It also incorporates various tools from business analytics. The module covers business valuation in distress situations.

module_catalog.name: Mini-dissertation 892
module_catalog.content: This module equips the student to conduct independent research by executing a research project on a relevant topic, of which the findings are reported in an academic article.

module_catalog.name: Research methodology 801
module_catalog.content: Planning and organising a research project Drafting a research proposal: Hypotheses and research question Theory in research and methodological approaches to legal research Language Citation and ethics of citation Drafting of chapters and presentation

module_catalog.name: Research proposal 803
module_catalog.content: Development and presentation of a research  proposal. (A research proposal must be submitted to the supervisor and accepted in the first semester of the second year of study  before the student will be allowed to register for the mini-dissertation.)
